articles.title: Gandhi Jayanti: Bapuji’s memorial statue in Odisha lies exposed amid neglect
articles.description: As the country observes Gandhi Jayanti and remembers Mahatma Gandhi and Lal Bahadur Shastri, questions have been raised over the condition of Odisha’s historic Gandhi Smruti Peetha near Pipili, a site associated with the memory of the Father of the Nation. The Smruti Peetha at Beraboi, Delanga block of Puri district, currently presents a picture of neglect. Two statues of Gandhiji stand on the premises, with one placed under a tin shed and the other exposed to the open sky. The exposed statue appears poorly maintained, with plastic a sheet tied around its feet and a cement bag wrapped around its neck. The steel staircase leading to the statue has also been covered with overgrown plants and creepers. The condition has raised concerns about the upkeep of a site associated with Gandhi’s legacy of truth, non-violence and humanity. Local residents have reportedly been demanding the development of the Gandhi memorial site for years. However, allegations persist that there has been little visible improvement despite the demands. After the new BJP-led government came to power in Odisha, a fresh tender was issued through OTDC for development work at the site. The work began but was subsequently halted. Signs of incomplete construction can now be seen across the premises, with grass and vegetation growing over several unfinished sections. A security guard deployed at the site said the work was stopped due to opposition from locals. However, no response was available from OTDC or the agency entrusted with the development work. At Beraboi ashram, the Father of the Nation had stayed from March 25 to 31, 1938. During this time, the fourth session of Gandhi Seva Sangh and Utkal Khadi Gramodyog exhibition were held. Since then, this place has been admired as Gandhi Smruti Peetha. “Gandhi's legacy is being neglected, with little work being undertaken to preserve his memory. This is due to a lack of political will power among leaders and a lack of interest among residents. Although a new statue has been installed, it has been placed under an asbestos roof, which is highly unfortunate. This reflects how Gandhi has been pushed to the last page of public attention,” a local man, Pradyumna Parida, told OTV. “A lot needs to be done for the Gandhi Smruti Peetha. Those who say the site is neglected are focusing only on the lack of construction, but there are two aspects that need attention—physical development and the preservation of Gandhiji’s ideology,” another resident and intelligentsia, Kabitarani Parida, stated. “The construction work has remained pending for years, making the site difficult to access. The work should be completed at the earliest to facilitate the establishment of cottage industries envisioned by Gandhiji and promote self-reliance among locals. Such initiatives would help preserve and carry forward Gandhi’s ideology,” Kabitarani added.

articles.title: Bengal to launch statewide survey to identify, reclaim encroached govt vested land
articles.description: Kolkata, Oct 2 (IANS) The West Bengal government is set to undertake a comprehensive survey of government-vested land across the state to identify encroachments and facilitate the recovery of illegally occupied plots, officials said. The West Bengal Land Records & Survey Directorate, which comes under the state land & land revenue department, will conduct the statewide survey. A senior department official said the survey will determine the exact boundaries of each state government-vested land to find out how much government land has been encroached upon and how much is in the government's possession. “A decision had been taken to erect permanent poles or pillars along the boundaries to maintain the state government’s occupation of the recovered land,” the state land & land revenue department said. According to officials, although, as per records, there are huge plots of government-vested land, there is confusion over what percentage of that land is actually in the possession of the state government and what percentage has been encroached upon. “There are reports that vested land under the jurisdiction of several state government departments, which had been lying idle for years, was gradually encroached upon over a period of time either by individual encroachers or by institutional encroachers. Now, as the new state government is approaching to attract big-ticket investments by announcing the new land policy, that initiative would require huge plots of land at one go. Hence, the survey is being conducted to identify and reclaim the encroached vested lands in the state,” said the department official. The Bengal Land Records & Survey Directorate had already floated a request for proposal or tender to get the work going by appointing an expert agency. “Once the survey is completed, it will be easier for the administration to determine the exact location, size and boundaries of government-vested land,” the state government official said. For this purpose, the department will use the sophisticated global navigation satellite systems to make the process absolutely accurate. The state government had also set a deadline to complete the survey process within the next six months. --IANS src/skp
